title: The Law of Love in Our Home
subtitle: Thomas Watson — The Ten Commandments
description: Thomas Watson opens his exposition of the Ten Commandments by showing how the first commandment — having no other gods — shapes the worship and priorities of the Christian family. Discover what it means to enthrone God in your home.
memoryVerse: Thou shalt have no other gods before me. -- Exodus 20:3
discussionQuestions: God introduces the Ten Commandments by reminding Israel of their redemption. Why does He begin with grace before giving law?
Thomas Watson said that idolatry is giving anything the place that belongs to God alone. What are some subtle idols that families today might struggle with?
What would it look like for our family to put God more fully on the throne of our home this month?

title: Worshipping God in Spirit and Truth at Home
subtitle: Thomas Watson — The Ten Commandments
description: Watson guides families through the second commandment, exploring how God calls us to worship Him not according to our own invention but according to His Word. Learn how family worship shapes generations.
memoryVerse: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth. -- John 4:24
discussionQuestions: What is the difference between the first and second commandments? Why does God care not only about whom we worship but how we worship?
Watson warned about the consequences of parents' spiritual choices on future generations. What spiritual habits would you like to pass down?
How can our family make our worship more faithful to what Scripture teaches?

title: Speaking God's Name with Reverence
subtitle: Thomas Watson — The Ten Commandments
description: The third commandment brings God's law into the realm of speech. Watson shows how honoring God's name transforms the atmosphere of a home and calls families to sincerity in prayer and integrity in daily living.
memoryVerse: Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain. -- Exodus 20:7
discussionQuestions: Watson said we take God's name in vain not only by cursing but by speaking of Him carelessly. In what subtle ways might our family be guilty of this?
How can we create a home atmosphere where God's name is spoken with reverence and love?
What is the connection between how we speak God's name and how we live?

title: The Gift of Sabbath Rest for Families
subtitle: Thomas Watson — The Ten Commandments
description: Watson calls the Sabbath 'the market day of the soul.' Explore the fourth commandment and discover how setting apart one day for worship and rest renews the entire family for the week ahead.
memoryVerse: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. -- Exodus 20:8
discussionQuestions: Watson called the Sabbath 'the market day of the soul.' What do you think he meant by that?
What are the biggest obstacles to keeping a restful, worshipful Sabbath as a family?
If we were to redesign our Sundays to be more faithful to the fourth commandment, what would we change?

title: Honor Thy Father and Mother
subtitle: Thomas Watson — The Ten Commandments
description: The fifth commandment stands at the hinge of the Decalogue. Watson explores the honor children owe their parents and the responsibilities parents bear before God, showing how healthy families build healthy communities.
memoryVerse: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee. -- Exodus 20:12
discussionQuestions: Why did God place the commandment about family at the hinge point between duties to God and duties to others?
Watson said honoring parents means more than obedience — it includes reverence, gratitude, and care. Which is hardest for you?
Parents, how can you lead your family with both tenderness and truth?

title: Protecting Life and Nurturing Kindness
subtitle: Thomas Watson — The Ten Commandments
description: Watson follows Jesus in expanding the sixth commandment beyond physical violence to address anger, contempt, and harsh speech within the family. Learn how to create a home culture of kindness and life-giving words.
memoryVerse: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger. -- Proverbs 15:1
discussionQuestions: Jesus said anger and contemptuous speech violate the spirit of the sixth commandment. What does this teach us about words in our home?
Watson said the sixth commandment requires not just the absence of harm but the active pursuit of good. How can we build one another up?
Is there anyone in our family who needs to hear a word of encouragement or reconciliation tonight?

title: Faithfulness, Truth, and Contentment in the Home
subtitle: Thomas Watson — The Ten Commandments
description: Watson surveys the seventh through tenth commandments, drawing out lessons on marital faithfulness, honest dealings, truthful speech, and freedom from covetousness — the virtues that hold a family together.
memoryVerse: And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. -- Deuteronomy 6:5
discussionQuestions: Watson said faithfulness in marriage creates security for the whole family. Why is covenant-keeping so important for children?
The ninth commandment calls us to be truthful. What makes honesty difficult in family relationships?
The tenth commandment addresses covetousness. What do we tend to covet as a family, and how can we cultivate contentment?

title: God's Providence Over Your Family
subtitle: John Flavel — Providence and Family Trust
description: John Flavel introduces the doctrine of divine providence — God's governance of all events — and shows how this truth anchors families in seasons of uncertainty and change.
memoryVerse: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose. -- Romans 8:28
discussionQuestions: What is providence? How is it different from luck or chance?
Can you think of a time when something that seemed bad turned out to be part of God's good plan for us?
Flavel compared providence to embroidery — tangled on one side, beautiful on the other. How does this help you trust God?

title: When God's Plan Surprises Us
subtitle: John Flavel — Providence and Family Trust
description: Flavel teaches that God delights in working through unexpected means and timing. Explore how families can respond with faith when God's plan looks different from their own expectations.
memoryVerse: A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps. -- Proverbs 16:9
discussionQuestions: Can you think of a time when God's plan for our family was different from what we expected?
Joseph told his brothers, 'Ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.' How does this help us when something painful happens?
Flavel said faith is not a feeling but a decision to trust God's Word. What makes this decision difficult?

title: Trusting God in Family Trials
subtitle: John Flavel — Providence and Family Trust
description: Flavel addresses how the doctrine of providence sustains families through trials, showing that every difficulty is designed by God for a specific, redemptive purpose.
memoryVerse: That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ. -- 1 Peter 1:7
discussionQuestions: Why does God allow families to go through trials? What purposes might He have in our suffering?
Flavel said trials have a unique bonding power for families. Have you seen this in our own family?
What are Flavel's three practical counsels for families in trials? Which one does our family need most?

title: Providence and Daily Provision
subtitle: John Flavel — Providence and Family Trust
description: Flavel applies the doctrine of providence to one of the most practical areas of family life — daily provision. Learn how to replace anxiety about material needs with trust in God's faithful care.
memoryVerse: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. -- Matthew 6:33
discussionQuestions: Jesus said God feeds the birds and clothes the flowers. What is He teaching us about His care for our family?
Flavel said anxiety in parents infects the whole household. How can we replace worry with trust?
What are three specific things God has provided for our family this week?

title: Providence in the Ordinary Moments
subtitle: John Flavel — Providence and Family Trust
description: Flavel helps families see God's hand not only in dramatic events but in the quiet, ordinary moments that make up most of daily life — meals, conversations, bedtime routines, and morning rituals.
memoryVerse: Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways. -- Psalm 139:3
discussionQuestions: Flavel taught that God is present in the ordinary moments. What is one everyday moment you might see differently now?
The psalmist says God knows our 'downsitting and uprising.' How does it feel to know God cares about the smallest details?
How can our family practice daily thanksgiving to notice God's providence in the ordinary?

title: Providence and the Protection of Our Children
subtitle: John Flavel — Providence and Family Trust
description: Flavel speaks to every parent's deepest concern — the safety and well-being of children — showing how God's providence covers them with a care that surpasses any human protection.
memoryVerse: For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. -- Psalm 91:11
discussionQuestions: Why is it sometimes hard for parents to trust God with their children's safety?
Can you think of a time when God protected someone in our family providentially?
How can prayer help parents with the anxiety they feel for their children?

title: Building a Family Legacy of Trust
subtitle: John Flavel — Providence and Family Trust
description: Flavel closes the week by showing families how to build a multigenerational legacy of trust — telling the stories of God's faithfulness, keeping a providence journal, and teaching children to see God at work.
memoryVerse: We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done. -- Psalm 78:4
discussionQuestions: Psalm 78 says we should tell our children about God's works. What stories from our family history do we want to pass down?
Flavel suggested keeping a 'providence journal.' Would our family like to start one?
What is one lesson from this week with Flavel that you want to carry forward?

title: Holy Affections in the Home
subtitle: Jonathan Edwards — Religious Affections Applied to the Family
description: Jonathan Edwards introduces his great theme of religious affections — the deep, settled dispositions of the heart — and shows why genuine spiritual emotion is essential for a thriving family.
memoryVerse: Whom having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory. -- 1 Peter 1:8
discussionQuestions: Edwards said true religion consists in 'holy affections.' What is the difference between genuine affections and mere emotions?
How can our family devotional time cultivate genuine love for God rather than just going through the motions?
Edwards taught that true affections produce visible fruit. What fruits of love for God are visible in our family?

title: The Beauty of God and the Joy of the Family
subtitle: Jonathan Edwards — Religious Affections Applied to the Family
description: Edwards teaches that the foundation of all holy affections is the beauty of God. Discover how a family captivated by God's beauty becomes a family overflowing with genuine, lasting joy.
memoryVerse: O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him. -- Psalm 34:8
discussionQuestions: Edwards said the deepest source of joy is the beauty of God. What is one attribute of God that you find especially wonderful?
How can our family learn to look for God's beauty in everyday life?
If beholding the beauty of the Lord became our family's one desire, how would our daily life change?

title: True Humility in the Family
subtitle: Jonathan Edwards — Religious Affections Applied to the Family
description: Edwards identifies humility as one of the surest marks of genuine faith. Explore how the gospel produces a humility that transforms family relationships — replacing pride with service and self-giving love.
memoryVerse: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. -- Philippians 2:3
discussionQuestions: Edwards said seeing God's holiness produces humility. How does a vision of God's greatness change the way we see ourselves?
Paul wrote, 'Let each esteem other better than themselves.' What would this look like in our family this week?
Christ humbled Himself by becoming a servant. Where is God calling you to serve someone in our family?

title: A Tender Conscience in the Home
subtitle: Jonathan Edwards — Religious Affections Applied to the Family
description: Edwards teaches that a tender conscience — sensitive to sin and quick to repent — is a mark of genuine grace. Learn how confession and forgiveness create a healthy, grace-filled family culture.
memoryVerse: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me. -- Psalm 51:10
discussionQuestions: What is a 'tender conscience'? Why is it a sign of genuine faith rather than weakness?
How does seeing a parent apologize affect a child's understanding of confession and forgiveness?
Is there anything on anyone's conscience tonight that needs to be confessed and forgiven within our family?

title: Gracious Speech and Loving Words
subtitle: Jonathan Edwards — Religious Affections Applied to the Family
description: Edwards shows that genuine affections transform our speech. Explore how gracious words can create a home atmosphere filled with encouragement, kindness, and grace that ministers to every family member.
memoryVerse: Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers. -- Ephesians 4:29
discussionQuestions: Edwards said speech reveals the condition of the heart. What does the way we speak to one another at home reveal?
Paul said our words should 'minister grace.' What would it look like to speak one grace-filled sentence to each family member now?
What is one pattern of speech in our home that we would like to change this week?

title: Persevering Love in the Family
subtitle: Jonathan Edwards — Religious Affections Applied to the Family
description: Edwards identifies perseverance as the ultimate test of genuine affection. Discover how a love that endures through the ordinary and the difficult holds a family together when everything else threatens to pull it apart.
memoryVerse: Charity never faileth. -- 1 Corinthians 13:8a
discussionQuestions: Edwards said perseverance is the ultimate test of genuine affection. Why is it easier to love in exciting moments than ordinary ones?
Which quality of love in 1 Corinthians 13 does our family need most right now?
How does knowing that God's love for us never fails give us strength to love one another with persevering love?

title: A Family of Christian Practice
subtitle: Jonathan Edwards — Religious Affections Applied to the Family
description: Edwards concludes with the most important mark of genuine affection — Christian practice. The proof of true faith is a life of consistent, daily obedience that transforms the family from within.
memoryVerse: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves. -- James 1:22
discussionQuestions: Edwards said Christian practice is the chief evidence of genuine faith. Why is what we do more important than what we feel?
James warns against being 'hearers only.' In what areas of our faith are we better at hearing than doing?
What is one specific act of Christian practice our family will commit to this week?

title: The Rare Jewel of a Content Family
subtitle: Jeremiah Burroughs — The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment
description: Jeremiah Burroughs introduces the rare jewel of Christian contentment — 'a sweet, inward, quiet, gracious frame of spirit' — and shows how this virtue transforms the entire atmosphere of family life.
memoryVerse: I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. -- Philippians 4:11b
discussionQuestions: Burroughs defined contentment as 'a sweet, inward, quiet, gracious frame of spirit.' Which word stands out to you most?
Paul said he 'learned' to be content. What might the learning process look like for our family?
What are five blessings we can name right now that we sometimes take for granted?

title: The Mystery of Contentment
subtitle: Jeremiah Burroughs — The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment
description: Burroughs reveals the surprising, counterintuitive secret of contentment: it comes not from getting more but from drawing closer to Christ. Discover the 'mystery' that enables believers to be content in any circumstance.
memoryVerse: My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. -- 2 Corinthians 12:9
discussionQuestions: Burroughs said contentment is about 'bringing the heart down to the condition.' What does this mean practically?
Paul found strength in weakness. Can you think of a time when our family's weakness became an opportunity to experience God's strength?
Burroughs said content Christians find sweetness in every condition. What is one difficult circumstance where we might look for hidden grace?

title: Contentment vs. Comparison
subtitle: Jeremiah Burroughs — The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment
description: Burroughs addresses one of contentment's deadliest enemies — the habit of comparing ourselves with others. Learn how to break free from comparison's destructive grip and rest in God's unique provision for your family.
memoryVerse: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage. -- Psalm 16:6
discussionQuestions: In what areas is our family most tempted to compare ourselves with other families?
Burroughs said we only see the outside of other people's lives. How does remembering this help us resist comparison?
The psalmist said, 'The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places.' How is God's provision for our family pleasant and good?

title: Contentment in Seasons of Plenty
subtitle: Jeremiah Burroughs — The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment
description: Burroughs reveals a counterintuitive truth: contentment is needed not only in want but in plenty. Explore the spiritual dangers of prosperity and the disciplines that keep families faithful when times are good.
memoryVerse: When thou hast eaten and art full, then thou shalt bless the LORD thy God for the good land which he hath given thee. -- Deuteronomy 8:10
discussionQuestions: Why might contentment be harder in prosperity than in scarcity? What spiritual dangers does abundance bring?
Burroughs said generosity is an antidote to the spiritual dangers of wealth. How is our family doing in this area?
Moses told Israel, 'Beware that thou forget not the Lord.' What practices help our family stay close to God when times are good?

title: Contentment in Seasons of Want
subtitle: Jeremiah Burroughs — The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment
description: Burroughs guides families through the hardest test of contentment — seasons of genuine want and loss — showing how faith transforms scarcity into sufficiency and loss into deeper dependence on God.
memoryVerse: Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation. -- Habakkuk 3:18
discussionQuestions: Habakkuk rejoiced in God even when everything was gone. What made this possible?
Burroughs said we should practice 'spiritual arithmetic' — counting what we still have rather than what we have lost. What blessings remain?
How does the cross of Christ give us confidence that God will provide for us in every season?

title: The Evil of Murmuring
subtitle: Jeremiah Burroughs — The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment
description: Burroughs exposes the dark opposite of contentment — murmuring and complaining — showing why this common family habit is far more spiritually serious than we often realize, and how thanksgiving is the cure.
memoryVerse: Do all things without murmurings and disputings. -- Philippians 2:14
discussionQuestions: Burroughs said murmuring against our circumstances is really murmuring against God. Why is this so serious?
How is murmuring contagious in a family? Can you think of a time when one person's complaining affected the whole household?
What is one area where our family tends to complain? How can we replace that complaint with thanksgiving?

title: God Himself Is Our Contentment
subtitle: Jeremiah Burroughs — The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment
description: Burroughs arrives at the crown of his teaching: the ultimate source of contentment is not any circumstance or blessing but God Himself. A family that possesses God possesses everything.
memoryVerse: Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee. -- Psalm 73:25
discussionQuestions: Burroughs said the ultimate source of contentment is God Himself, not His gifts. What is the difference?
The psalmist declared, 'There is none upon earth that I desire beside thee.' What competes with God for our deepest desires?
What is the most important lesson about contentment you take away from this week with Burroughs?

title: A Summer of Puritan Wisdom
subtitle: Summer Synthesis — Carrying Puritan Wisdom into Summer
description: As June closes and summer opens, gather the treasures of the month — Watson's commandments, Flavel's providence, Edwards's affections, and Burroughs's contentment — and weave them into your family's summer rhythms.
memoryVerse: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way. -- Deuteronomy 6:7
discussionQuestions: Of the four Puritan teachers this month, which one's teaching resonated most deeply with you, and why?
Moses said to talk about God's truth everywhere. How can our family build spiritual conversations into our summer?
What is one practical way our family can keep growing spiritually this summer?

title: A Benediction for Summer
subtitle: Summer Synthesis — Carrying Puritan Wisdom into Summer
description: The final devotional of June sends the family forth with a benediction — the Aaronic blessing — and a recapitulation of the month's four great themes, commissioning the family for a summer of faithfulness and joy.
memoryVerse: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace. -- Numbers 6:24-26
discussionQuestions: As we look back over this entire month, what is the single truth or moment that stands out most to each family member?
How has our family changed through these thirty days of devotion together?
What commitment do we want to make as a family for the summer ahead?
